But in what sense is it meant that a true judgment takes
place, to which the Spirit opens the eyes of the Christian?
The Spirit will convict the world of "sin and righteousness
and judgment"; i.e. the Spirit will show what these three
words in truth mean, and, at the same time, who is the
sinner, who the righteous man, and who is judged. The
world also is of course familiar with these three words; it
speaks about sin and justice and judgment and supposes it
knows what they mean.
The world understands by sin, moral failings and guilty
deeds. It does not hesitate to condemn sin; nevertheless it
does not take sin seriously. It thinks of sin as of something
occasional, fortuitous, a deviation which might possibly
occur. It does not realize that if anyone sins he is the slave of
sin (John 8: 34). And if anyone suggests that the world is
sinful, it derides him or is angry. For it is of the very essence
of the self-consciousness and need of the world, that it should
consider itself to be right and good. It holds the question of
sin to be a question which it has to decide and settle from
within its own sphere, before its own forum and according
to its own law. And it does not realize that the word "sin"
presupposes a reference to a judge beyond the world; it is
unfamiliar with the concept of God's consuming holiness.
The recognition inspired by the Spirit is this: it will
convict the world of sin because "they do not believe on me".
The sin of the world consists in unbelief rather than in any
particular wanton misdeed. Scripture does not for example
say: "because they have crucified me". The sin of the world
is not for example that it failed to recognize in Jesus a noble
man and brought Him to the cross. The text says: "because
they do not believe on me. It does not say: "because they
have not believed" but "because they do not believe". It is
not a question of any particular piece of conduct but of the
characteristic basic attitude of the world, an attitude which
